newsitem.title: CHINA: China may implement soybean import quota in '97.
newsitem.headline: China may implement soybean import quota in '97.

text.p: China could put into effect next year quotas on soybean imports, an official of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation said on Thursday.

The cabinet's State Planning Commission had issued regulations in April imposing quotas on soybean imports along with several other farm products, but they had yet to go into effect, the official said by telephone.
The official said that imports within the quota would be subject to normal duties. Imports above that level would be permitted but duties would be set at a higher rate.

The official said he expected the quotas to go into effect sometime in 1997, although he declined to say precisely when or give the size. He also declined to specify the level of duties or give other details.
